analysis: The changes are documentation-only: docs/developer/build.md (CI runner routing and job-size prose, e.g. lines 379-396, 569-596, 619-628) and docs/developer/test.md (lines 2057-2058). They remove 'required' markings from the build jobs and Cluster Release Build Checks, and state that with job sizes off every routed lane asks without a size and gets the approval's pinned macOS size. They also note that a `required` lane keeps its fallback without asking. No code, workflow, provider, coordinator, attestation, key, or cache-storage behavior changes in the supplied units. None of the changes touches the provider threat-model assets or boundaries (TB-002/003/007/009/011/012, A-001 to A-020) or the T-041 cache posture, and the text does not weaken any stated control. Release, signing and publication jobs are still documented as keeping literal Blacksmith labels. The CI cache save-policy text (pushes to master and dev only) is unchanged. One residual question is outside the supplied evidence: the actual workflow lane table in provider-plan.yml and provider-tests.yml was not provided. Running build jobs on routed Darkbloom Sandbox runners rather than Blacksmith is a CI supply-chain surface, but this PR's supplied diff only documents it. Whether the docs match the workflow YAML needs the workflow diff, which is not in this batch. The docs state that routed jobs are read-only, fork PRs keep their fallback, and grants must match the exact labels. I found no evidence of a security regression.
